blurb: Read-only. Draw and measure the maps of Fallout 1, Fallout 2 and the total conversions, so a new map starts from how real ones are built.

Render close-ups of the vignettes tools/story_survey.py found, so the scenes can be studied by eye.

blurb: Search the games for art, protos, tiles, buildings and rooms; build the fragment corpus and the art index.

What art exists for a thing, across every source, with its cost.
Find buildings, in any source's maps, walled in given wall families (e.g.
Search FOC's protos by display name or art name.
List the rooms of any source level, so compose_map.py can lift single rooms instead of whole levels.
Search every source game's item names (pro_item.msg) for words, to find something to port with port_item.py.
List FOC floor/roof tile ids by name prefix (ids below 4096, the only ones gecko and the engine can address).

blurb: Draw a map to scale on paper before placing anything: the real place, the game references, the plan.

Fetch a real place's layout from OpenStreetMap (Overpass API) and draw it to scale, north up, as the reference a FOC site plan is adapted from.

blurb: Compose a map from a recipe, from stamps, from a grid, or from code; make stamps from the originals' buildings.

Design a FOC map in code and write it as a compose_map.py recipe.
Write a valid Fallout 2 .map from scratch.
Compile a data-first map grid (JSON) into a Fallout 2 .map.

blurb: Edges, scroll blockers, exits, links, trimming and cleanup, the way Fallout 2 does them.

tools.what: Give FOC's maps Hi-Res Patch edge files (maps/<name>.edg), so the camera stops at the edge of the painted ground and the void beyond is never seen.
Stop the player walking into the black edge of a map.
Replace a map's scroll-blocker ring with one sized to the map's actual content, so the camera can't be scrolled out past it into undecorated wasteland or the void beyond.

Rebuild every exit-grid patch on FOC maps the way Fallout, Fallout 2 and the TCs lay them out.
Rebuild a map's exit-grid ring at the edge of its painted floor.

Bind a script to one specific object on a map, by tile.

blurb: Browse another game in gecko, save stamps, and convert them into your mod's id space; port protos and art; make your own scenery.

tools.what: Generate tools/gecko_browse/, one launcher per TC.
Pull assets in from another Fallout 2 install and remap them into this project's ID space.

New floor and roof tiles for FOC, in slots of tiles.lst that hold nothing FOC can lose.
Move every piece of FOC art that something actually uses below the engine's 4096 art-index cap, swapping unused art up past it.
Bring every FOC art filename within the engine's 12-char limit.
Make the FOnline 2 client usable as an asset source, like the TC installs, without repeating anything we already have.

blurb: Allocate ids, assemble the game's lists, register the map on the world map, check cross-references and deploy into the working copy of the game.

tools.what: The project's ID space.
Turn mod/ids/*.txt into the generated header scripts_src/foc/foc_ids.h.
Assemble the .lst / .gam files the game actually loads.
Build the Pip-Boy quest log (data\quests.txt) from mod/quests.txt.
Register FOC maps with the engine (maps.txt / city.txt / map.msg) and fit worldmap.txt to FOC's West Texas worldmap art.
Check the mod's ID space and cross-references before it ever runs.
Assemble the mod into the working base install so it can be played.
Install an upstream sfall release into the working base.
